symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of sampled units.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: The number of balanced-panel periods.

symbols.name: time_set
symbols.def: \(\mathcal T=\{1,\ldots,T\}\).

symbols.name: adoption_set
symbols.def: \(\mathcal G=\{2,\ldots,T\}\) is the set of admissible enabling dates, so every treated cohort has an observed baseline period \(g-1\in\mathcal T\).

symbols.name: eligibility_index
symbols.def: \(s\) indexes treatment eligibility.

symbols.name: cohort_index
symbols.def: \(a\) indexes an enabling cohort.

symbols.name: treated_cohort
symbols.def: \(g\in\mathcal G\) indexes a cohort whose effect is targeted and always has the observed baseline \(g-1\in\mathcal T\).

symbols.name: post_period
symbols.def: \(t\) indexes a post-enabling outcome period.

symbols.name: comparison_cohort
symbols.def: \(c\) indexes a cohort not yet enabled at the target period.

symbols.name: X_space
symbols.def: \(\mathcal X\) is the support of pretreatment covariates.

symbols.name: covariate_value
symbols.def: \(x\in\mathcal X\).

symbols.name: X_i
symbols.def: \(X_i\) is unit \(i\)'s observed pretreatment covariate.

symbols.name: G_i
symbols.def: \(G_i\) is unit \(i\)'s first enabling date, with \(\infty\) denoting never enabled.

symbols.name: S_i
symbols.def: \(S_i\) is unit \(i\)'s time-invariant eligibility status.

symbols.name: Y_pot
symbols.def: \(Y_{it}(a,s)\) is the period-\(t\) outcome under enabling date \(a\) and eligibility state \(s\).

symbols.name: Y_obs
symbols.def: The balanced observed outcome history for unit \(i\).

symbols.name: W_i
symbols.def: \(W_i=(\{Y_{it}(a,s):t\in\mathcal T,a\in\mathcal G\cup\{\infty\},s\in\{0,1\}\},Y_i,G_i,S_i,X_i)\) carries every potential outcome, the observed outcome history, enabling date, eligibility, and pretreatment covariates.

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: \(Q\) is the common full-data law of \(W_i\).

symbols.name: observation_map
symbols.def: \(o(W_i)=(Y_i,G_i,S_i,X_i)\) discards the unobserved potential-outcome coordinates.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: \(P=Q_O=Q\circ o^{-1}\) is the observed-data pushforward of the full-data law under the observation map.

symbols.name: cell_probability
symbols.def: \(p_{a,s}(x)=P(G_i=a,S_i=s\mid X_i=x)\).

symbols.name: group_event_index
symbols.def: \(k=(g,t)\) denotes a treated group-period cell with \(2\le g\le t\le T\); hence the baseline \(g-1\) and post period \(t\) are both in \(\mathcal T\).

symbols.name: target_set
symbols.def: \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal K\subseteq\{(g,t):2\le g\le t\le T\}\) is the prespecified support of the event-study aggregate.

symbols.name: comparison_set
symbols.def: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal J_k\subseteq\{c\in\mathcal G\cup\{\infty\}:c>t\}\) is the prespecified set of retained not-yet-enabled comparison cohorts.

symbols.name: score_dimension
symbols.def: \(M=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}|\mathcal J_k|\).

symbols.name: outcome_change
symbols.def: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\) with \(2\le g\le t\le T\), \(\Delta Y_{i,k}=Y_{it}-Y_{i,g-1}\); in the boundary cohort \(g=2\), this is \(Y_{it}-Y_{i1}\).

symbols.name: outcome_regression
symbols.def: \(m_{a,s,k}(x)=E_P[\Delta Y_{i,k}\mid G_i=a,S_i=s,X_i=x]\).

symbols.name: ddd_contrast
symbols.def: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), and \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), \(d_{k,c}(x)=m_{g,1,k}(x)-m_{g,0,k}(x)-m_{c,1,k}(x)+m_{c,0,k}(x)\).

symbols.name: residual_covariance
symbols.def: \(v_{a,s;k\ell}(x)=E_P[(\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(x))(\Delta Y_{i,\ell}-m_{a,s,\ell}(x))\mid G_i=a,S_i=s,X_i=x]\).

symbols.name: nuisance_vector
symbols.def: \(\eta_0\) stacks all \(p_{a,s}\) and \(m_{a,s,k}\) entering the retained comparisons.

symbols.name: ATT_vector
symbols.def: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), \(\theta_k(Q)=E_Q[Y_{it}(g,1)-Y_{it}(\infty,1)\mid G_i=g,S_i=1]\).

symbols.name: observable_ATT_vector
symbols.def: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), \[\Theta_k(P)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal J_k|}\sum_{c\in\mathcal J_k}\frac{E_P[p_{g,1}(X_i)d_{k,c}(X_i)]}{\pi_{g,1}}.\]

symbols.name: aggregate_weights
symbols.def: \(\omega\) fixes the reported event-study aggregation before observing outcomes.

symbols.name: tau
symbols.def: \(\tau_\omega(Q)=\omega^{\prime}\theta(Q)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\theta_k(Q)\).

symbols.name: observable_aggregate
symbols.def: \(\Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)=\omega^{\prime}\Theta(P)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\Theta_k(P)\).

symbols.name: cell_sign
symbols.def: \(\sigma_{g,1}^{g,c}=1\), \(\sigma_{g,0}^{g,c}=-1\), \(\sigma_{c,1}^{g,c}=-1\), \(\sigma_{c,0}^{g,c}=1\), and the sign is zero otherwise.

symbols.name: score_residual_loading
symbols.def: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and \(a\in\{g,c\}\), \(L_{k,c}^{a,s}(x)=p_{g,1}(x)\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}/\{\pi_{g,1}p_{a,s}(x)\}\).

symbols.name: pairwise_score
symbols.def: The ratio-adjusted doubly robust pseudo-outcome defined in \(\mathrm{Def.}\) \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\).

symbols.name: stacked_score
symbols.def: \(R(O_i;\eta_0)=(R_{k,c}(O_i;\eta_0):(k,c)\in\mathcal I)^{\prime}\), where \(\mathcal I=\{(k,c):k\in\mathcal K,c\in\mathcal J_k\}\).

symbols.name: incidence_matrix
symbols.def: \(B_{(k,c),\ell}=\mathbf 1\{k=\ell\}\), so each row selects the ATT identified by that pairwise score.

symbols.name: centered_score
symbols.def: \(\Psi(O_i)=R(O_i;\eta_0)-B\Theta(P)\), whose coordinates include the target-share ratio correction in \(\mathrm{Def.}\) \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\).

symbols.name: score_covariance
symbols.def: \(\Omega=E_P[\Psi(O_i)\Psi(O_i)^{\prime}]\), partitioned into blocks \(\Omega_{k\ell}\) conformably with \(\mathcal J_k\) and \(\mathcal J_\ell\).

symbols.name: ddd_covariance
symbols.def: The primitive shared-cell covariance construction in \(\mathrm{Def.}\) \(\ref{def:shared-covariance}\).

symbols.name: contrast_matrix
symbols.def: Order each \(\mathcal J_k=\{c_{k,1}<\cdots<c_{k,J_k}\}\), with \(\infty\) last when present, and set \(N=\operatorname{diag}(N_k:k\in\mathcal K)\), where \(N_k=[e_1-e_{J_k},\ldots,e_{J_k-1}-e_{J_k}]\). Thus \(N\) is a canonical full-column-rank zero-sum contrast basis determined by the labelled comparison sets and satisfies \(B^{\prime}N=0\).

symbols.name: separate_weight
symbols.def: The componentwise GMM loading defined in \(\mathrm{Def.}\) \(\ref{def:separate-loading}\).

symbols.name: joint_weight
symbols.def: The joint aggregate GMM loading defined in \(\mathrm{Def.}\) \(\ref{def:joint-loading}\).

symbols.name: separate_variance
symbols.def: \(V_{\mathrm{sep}}=(b^{\mathrm{sep}})^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}\).

symbols.name: joint_variance
symbols.def: \(V_{\mathrm{joint}}=(b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{joint}}\).

symbols.name: number_folds
symbols.def: The fixed number of cross-fitting folds.

symbols.name: fold_map
symbols.def: \(f(i)\) assigns unit \(i\) to one of \(F\) folds whose sizes differ by at most one.

symbols.name: moment_constant
symbols.def: A common fourth-moment bound.

symbols.name: spectrum_constant
symbols.def: A common covariance-eigenvalue bound.

symbols.name: propensity_l4_rate
symbols.def: The fold-uniform \(L_4(P_X)\) rate for raw cell-propensity fits, with \(a_n\to0\).

symbols.name: regression_l4_rate
symbols.def: The fold-uniform \(L_4(P_X)\) rate for outcome-regression fits, with \(b_n\to0\) and \(a_nb_n=o(n^{-1/2})\).

symbols.name: ridge_sequence
symbols.def: \(\lambda_n=n^{-1/4}\) is the strictly positive covariance ridge.

symbols.name: test_level
symbols.def: The two-sided Wald test size.

symbols.name: normal_quantile
symbols.def: \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) is the \(1-\alpha/2\) quantile of \(N(0,1)\).

symbols.name: estimated_nuisance
symbols.def: \(\widehat\eta_{-f(i)}\) stacks real-valued raw fits \(\widehat p_{a,s,-f(i)}\) and \(\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}\) trained without fold \(f(i)\).

symbols.name: score_coordinate_set
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I=\{j=(k,c):k\in\mathcal K,\ c\in\mathcal J_k\}\) is the labelled set of retained pairwise-score coordinates.

symbols.name: primitive_residual_set
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R=\{\rho=(a,s,u):\text{ for some }j=((g,t),c)\in\mathcal I,\;a\in\{g,c\},\;s\in\{0,1\},\;u\in\{g-1,t\}\}\) records every observed cohort, eligibility, and time coordinate underlying a retained outcome-change residual.

symbols.name: signed_incidence_tensor
symbols.def: For \(j=((g,t),c)\in\mathcal I\) and \(\rho=(a,s,u)\in\mathcal R\), set \[A_{j\rho}(x)=L_{(g,t),c}^{a,s}(x)\mathbf 1\{a\in\{g,c\}\}\{\mathbf 1(u=t)-\mathbf 1(u=g-1)\}.\] This records the score label, admissible comparison label, cohort-eligibility-time residual cell, and its signed coefficient.

symbols.name: compatible_covariance_map
symbols.def: For \(j=(k,c)\) and \(q=(\ell,d)\), \(C_{jq}(P)\) is the right-hand side of the primitive shared-cell formula in \(\mathrm{Def.}\) \(\ref{def:shared-covariance}\), including both the target-cell contrast covariance and every residual covariance entry induced by the signed incidences \(A_{j\rho}\) and \(A_{q\rho'}\). Thus \(\mathfrak C(P)=\Omega(P)\) for compatible observed-data laws.

symbols.name: labelled_reuse_invariant
symbols.type: law-indexed labelled multigraph and incidence invariant
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak H(P)=(\mathcal I,(\mathcal J_k)_{k\in\mathcal K},\mathcal R,A,\omega,\mathfrak C(P),N)\) retains every score coordinate \(j=(k,c)\), every admissible comparison label, every cohort-eligibility-time residual coordinate, every signed incidence coefficient, the prespecified aggregate weights, all compatible covariance-map entries needed to recover \(\Omega(P)\), and the canonical contrast matrix. Two invariants are equivalent only when there are label-preserving bijections under which all seven components, including \(A\), \(\omega\), \(\mathfrak C\), and \(N\), agree exactly.

symbols.name: retained_cell_count
symbols.def: Define the fixed retained cohort-eligibility cell set by \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ret}}=\{(a,s):s\in\{0,1\},\ \exists k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K,\ c\in\mathcal J_k,\ a\in\{g,c\}\}\), and set \(L_{\mathrm{ret}}=|\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ret}}|\).

symbols.name: overlap_constant
symbols.def: A feasible common lower bound for all distinct retained cohort-eligibility cells in the fixed design.

symbols.name: clipping_map
symbols.def: \(C_\varepsilon(u)=\min\{1-\varepsilon/2,\max\{\varepsilon/2,u\}\}\).

symbols.name: clipped_propensity
symbols.def: \(\widetilde p_{a,s,-f(i)}(x)=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{a,s,-f(i)}(x))\).

symbols.name: clipped_target_probability
symbols.def: \(\widetilde\pi_{g,1}=C_\varepsilon(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\})\).

symbols.name: fitted_influence
symbols.def: The everywhere-defined cross-fitted influence vector displayed in \(\mathrm{Def.}\) \(\ref{def:joint-estimator}\).

symbols.name: score_mean_estimator
symbols.def: The vector of cross-fitted Hájek-ratio pairwise DDD estimators defined in \(\mathrm{Def.}\) \(\ref{def:joint-estimator}\).

symbols.name: raw_covariance_estimator
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat\Psi_i\widehat\Psi_i^{\prime}\).

symbols.name: covariance_estimator
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Omega=\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^M}(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}})\), where \(\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^M}\) is the unique Frobenius-norm projection onto the positive-semidefinite cone.

symbols.name: regularized_covariance_estimator
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Omega_{\lambda}=\widehat\Omega+\lambda_n I_M\), which is positive definite for every realized sample.

symbols.name: estimated_separate_weight
symbols.def: For each \(k\), \(\widehat b_k^{\mathrm{sep}}=\omega_k\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1/(\mathbf 1^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1)\), and the blocks are stacked.

symbols.name: estimated_joint_weight
symbols.def: \(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}=\widehat\Omega_{\lambda}^{-1}B(B^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_{\lambda}^{-1}B)^{-1}\omega\).

symbols.name: joint_estimator
symbols.def: The feasible joint aggregate estimator defined in \(\mathrm{Def.}\) \(\ref{def:joint-estimator}\).

symbols.name: separate_estimator
symbols.def: The feasible componentwise-GMM plug-in aggregate defined in \(\mathrm{Def.}\) \(\ref{def:joint-estimator}\).

symbols.name: joint_variance_estimator
symbols.def: \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\widehat\Omega\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}\), using the projected but unridged covariance.

symbols.name: wald_interval
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_{n,1-\alpha}=[\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}-z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}/n},\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}+z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}/n}]\); when \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}=0\), its standard error is defined as zero and the interval is the singleton \(\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}\}\).

symbols.name: estimated_variance_gap
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Delta=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\widehat\Omega(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})\) is the feasible diagnostic for the constant-score-span variance loss.

assumptions.condition: \(W_1,\ldots,W_n\) are independent draws from \(Q\), with fixed \(T\).
\(Q\{Y_{it}(g,1)=Y_{it}(\infty,1)\text{ for every }g\in\mathcal G\text{ and }t\in\mathcal T\text{ with }t<g\}=1\).

standard.name: No treatment effect on ineligible units

assumptions.condition: For every \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\) with \(2\le g\le t\le T\), every \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and \(Q_X\)-almost every \(x\), \(E_Q[Y_{it}(\infty,1)-Y_{i,g-1}(\infty,1)\mid G_i=g,S_i=1,X_i=x]-E_Q[Y_{it}(\infty,0)-Y_{i,g-1}(\infty,0)\mid G_i=g,S_i=0,X_i=x]=E_Q[Y_{it}(\infty,1)-Y_{i,g-1}(\infty,1)\mid G_i=c,S_i=1,X_i=x]-E_Q[Y_{it}(\infty,0)-Y_{i,g-1}(\infty,0)\mid G_i=c,S_i=0,X_i=x]\).
For every \((a,s)\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ret}}\), \(Q(G_i=a,S_i=s\mid X_i=x)\ge\varepsilon\) for \(Q_X\)-almost every \(x\), where \(0<\varepsilon<L_{\mathrm{ret}}^{-1}\).

For every fold \(f\), conditional on the training observations \(\{O_i:f(i)\ne f\}\), the off-fold fit \(\widehat\eta_{-f}\) is fixed and is independent of the validation observations \(\{O_i:f(i)=f\}\).
Conditional on the training samples, \(\max_{f,a,s}\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n)\) with \(a_n\to0\).
Conditional on the training samples, \(\max_{f,a,s,k}\|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(b_n)\) with \(b_n\to0\).

definitions.name: Staggered-DDD law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathsf W): Q\text{ satisfies consistency, no anticipation, no ineligible spillover, every retained pairwise conditional DDD restriction, cell overlap with }0<\varepsilon<L_{\mathrm{ret}}^{-1},\text{ and, for }P=Q_O,\text{ the outcome fourth-moment and score-spectrum bounds}\}\). The class contains only primitive restrictions on \(Q\) and its observed-data pushforward \(P\); conditional Jensen's inequality and overlap imply the needed true-regression moments. Independent sampling, cross-fitting, learner rates, and fitted-regression tightness are theorem-level conditions or consequences, not members of the law class.

definitions.name: Observed-data DDD functional
definitions.construction: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), define \[\Theta_k(P)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal J_k|}\sum_{c\in\mathcal J_k}\frac{E_P[p_{g,1}(X_i)d_{k,c}(X_i)]}{\pi_{g,1}},\qquad \Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)=\omega^{\prime}\Theta(P).\] Both quantities are functionals only of the observed-data law \(P=Q_O\).

definitions.name: Pairwise ratio-adjusted DDD score
definitions.construction: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), and \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), set \[R_{k,c}(O_i;\eta_0)=\Theta_k(P)+\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}}{\pi_{g,1}}\{d_{k,c}(X_i)-\Theta_k(P)\}+\frac{p_{g,1}(X_i)}{\pi_{g,1}}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{p_{a,s}(X_i)}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\}.\] Thus \(R_{k,c}-\Theta_k(P)\) is the observed-data first-order influence of the Hájek-ratio pairwise estimator, including estimation of \(\pi_{g,1}\).

definitions.name: Primitive shared-cell covariance matrix
definitions.construction: For score coordinates \(j=(k,c)\) and \(q=(\ell,d)\), let \(g_k\) and \(g_\ell\) denote the first components of \(k\) and \(\ell\), and define \[\Omega^{\mathrm{DDD}}_{j q}=E_P\!\left[\frac{\mathbf 1\{g_k=g_\ell\}p_{g_k,1}(X_i)\{d_{k,c}(X_i)-\Theta_k(P)\}\{d_{\ell,d}(X_i)-\Theta_\ell(P)\}}{\pi_{g_k,1}\pi_{g_\ell,1}}+\sum_{a,s}p_{a,s}(X_i)L_{k,c}^{a,s}(X_i)L_{\ell,d}^{a,s}(X_i)v_{a,s;k\ell}(X_i)\right].\] The sum ranges over cohort-eligibility cells entering both score coordinates.

definitions.name: Componentwise GMM aggregate loading
definitions.construction: For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \[(b^{\mathrm{sep}})_k=\omega_k\frac{\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1}{\mathbf 1^{\prime}\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1},\] and \(b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) stacks these blocks. This is exactly the loading produced by optimizing each group-event cell separately and then applying \(\omega\).

definitions.name: Feasible separate and joint estimators
definitions.construction:
For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and observation \(i\), first set \(\widetilde p_{a,s,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{a,s,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde p_{g,1,i}=C_\varepsilon(\widehat p_{g,1,-f(i)}(X_i))\), \(\widetilde\pi_{g,1}=C_\varepsilon(n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbf 1\{G_j=g,S_j=1\})\), and \(\widehat d_{k,c,i}=\widehat m_{g,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{g,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)-\widehat m_{c,1,k,-f(i)}(X_i)+\widehat m_{c,0,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\). Define \[\widehat A_{i,k,c}=\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\widehat d_{k,c,i}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\},\qquad \widehat\mu_{k,c}=\frac{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat A_{i,k,c}}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}},\] and display the fitted influence coordinate \[\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}=\frac{1}{\widetilde\pi_{g,1}}\left[\mathbf 1\{G_i=g,S_i=1\}\{\widehat d_{k,c,i}-\widehat\mu_{k,c}\}+\widetilde p_{g,1,i}\sum_{(a,s)\in\{g,c\}\times\{0,1\}}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}\frac{\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}}{\widetilde p_{a,s,i}}\{\Delta Y_{i,k}-\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f(i)}(X_i)\}\right].\] Stack \(\widehat\mu_{k,c}\) and \(\widehat\Psi_{i,k,c}\). Set \(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}=n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_i\widehat\Psi_i^{\prime}\), \(\widehat\Omega=\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^M}(\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}})\), and \(\widehat\Omega_\lambda=\widehat\Omega+n^{-1/4}I_M\). For each \(k\), set \(\widehat b_k^{\mathrm{sep}}=\omega_k\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1/(\mathbf 1^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_{\lambda,kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1)\), and set \(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}=\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B(B^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B)^{-1}\omega\). Finally, \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sep}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}})^{\prime}\widehat\mu\), \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\widehat\mu\), and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\widehat\Omega\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}\). Define the feasible constant-score-span efficiency-loss diagnostic by
\[
\widehat\Delta=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}
\widehat\Omega
(\widehat b^{\mathrm{sep}}-\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}).
\]
Every denominator and inverse in this construction is defined for every realized sample, and \(\widehat\Delta\ge0\) because \(\widehat\Omega\) is positive semidefinite.

definitions.name: Studentized joint-GMM Wald interval
definitions.construction: Let \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) be the \(1-\alpha/2\) quantile of \(N(0,1)\) and define \[\mathcal C_{n,1-\alpha}=\left[\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}-z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}/n},\;\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}+z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}/n}\right].\] If \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}=0\), define the estimated standard error to be zero, do not divide by it, and set \(\mathcal C_{n,1-\alpha}=\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}\}\).

definitions.name: Sufficient labelled shared-cell invariant
definitions.construction: Expand every score coordinate \(j=((g,t),c)\in\mathcal I\) into the cohort-eligibility-time residual coordinates \(\rho=(a,s,u)\in\mathcal R\), attach the signed functional coefficient \(A_{j\rho}(x)\), and retain \(\mathfrak H(P)=(\mathcal I,(\mathcal J_k)_k,\mathcal R,A,\omega,\mathfrak C(P),N)\). Recover \(\Omega(P)=\mathfrak C(P)\), compute the published componentwise loading blockwise, and evaluate \(N^{\prime}\Omega(P)b^{\mathrm{sep}}(P)\). Classify only label-preserving equivalence classes for which the comparison labels, residual labels, signed incidences, aggregate weights, covariance-map entries, and canonical contrast matrix all agree. For the smallest strict-gap search, specialize to \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2),(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3,\infty\}\), and \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{\infty\}\); parameterize bounded cell residuals and target-cell contrasts, enforce the causal restrictions, compute the resulting \(3\times3\) positive-definite \(\Omega\), and determine the variance-gap quadratic form exactly.

statements.statement: The primitive law class is nonempty for a feasible common overlap constant. Take \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3\}\), \(\omega_{(2,2)}=1\), \(\varepsilon=1/8\), \(C_4=1\), and \(\kappa=1/2\). Let \(X_i=x_0\) almost surely; let \((G_i,S_i)\) be uniform on \(\{(2,0),(2,1),(3,0),(3,1)\}\); and independently let \(U_{i1},U_{i2},U_{i3}\) be independent Rademacher variables. Set \(Y_{it}(a,s)=U_{it}/8\) for every \(a\in\{2,3,\infty\}\), \(s\in\{0,1\}\), and \(t\in\{1,2,3\}\), and set \(Y_{it}=Y_{it}(G_i,S_i)\). The induced full-data law \(Q_0\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\): all four retained disjoint cells have probability \(1/4>\varepsilon\), the causal restrictions hold with zero effects and common trends, \(m_{a,s,(2,2)}=0\), and the sole centered score equals \(4\sigma_{a,s}^{2,3}\{U_{i2}-U_{i1}\}/8\) on cell \((a,s)\). Consequently, \(\Omega=1/2\), so \(\kappa I_1\preceq\Omega\preceq\kappa^{-1}I_1\), while the outcome and true-regression fourth-moment bounds hold.
statements.justification: The explicit bounded four-cell construction proves that the feasible overlap and positive-spectrum requirements do not empty the model.
statements.gap: This is a supporting well-posedness witness, not a novelty claim against the staggered-DDD literature.
statements.consumer: Every theorem quantifying over \(\mathcal M\) has a concrete compatible data-generating law with \(g=2\) and a defined baseline.

statements.statement: For every full-data law \(Q\in\mathcal M\), let \(P=Q_O=Q\circ o^{-1}\). For every \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), where \(2\le g\le t\le T\), and every \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), \[\theta_k(Q)=\frac{E_P[p_{g,1}(X_i)d_{k,c}(X_i)]}{\pi_{g,1}}=E_P[R_{k,c}(O_i;\eta_0)].\] Consequently, \(\theta(Q)=\Theta(P)\), \(\tau_\omega(Q)=\Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)\), \(E_P[R(O_i;\eta_0)]=B\Theta(P)\), and \(E_P[\Psi(O_i)]=0\). For the earliest admissible cohort \(g=2\), every displayed change uses the defined baseline \(g-1=1\).
statements.justification: This published identification reduction fixes the exact score system whose cross-cell information is compared.
statements.gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna prove the underlying pairwise DDD identification; the lemma is supporting structure and is not claimed as novel.
statements.consumer: The joint GMM theorem uses the observable common-mean restriction \(E_P[R]=B\Theta(P)\) while its Wald interval targets the causal aggregate \(\tau_\omega(Q)\).

statements.statement: For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with observed-data law \(P=Q_O\), \(\Omega=\Omega^{\mathrm{DDD}}\). In particular, the residual part of \(\Omega_{(k,c),(\ell,d)}\) contains a primitive cell \((a,s)\) if and only if that cohort-eligibility cell enters both pairwise scores; covariance across distinct observed cells vanishes by mutual exclusivity, while repeated outcome histories within a shared cell enter through \(v_{a,s;k\ell}(X_i)\).
statements.justification: This expansion is the DDD-specific step that converts generic systems covariance into shared eligible and ineligible comparison-cell information.
statements.gap: Neither generic GMM nor seemingly unrelated regressions records the mutually exclusive cohort-eligibility cells and repeated panel outcome changes that determine staggered-DDD cross-block covariance.
statements.consumer: The frontier diagnostic can be computed from cellwise residual covariances without treating comparison-cohort estimates as independent.

statements.statement: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\mathcal K\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with \(P=Q_O\), suppose the off-fold learners satisfy foldwise independence, \(\max_{f,a,s}\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n)\), \(\max_{f,a,s,k}\|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(b_n)\), \(a_n\to0\), \(b_n\to0\), and \(a_nb_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). These learner sequences and rates are theorem-level conditional hypotheses; no uniform learner-achievability claim over \(\mathcal M\) is made. Four disjoint cells enter each retained pairwise score, so overlap and \(0<\varepsilon<1/4\) give \(p_{a,s}(x)\in[\varepsilon,1-3\varepsilon]\subset[\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]\) for every retained cell. Hence \(C_\varepsilon(p_{a,s})=p_{a,s}\), the clipping map is one-Lipschitz, and \[\|\widetilde p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}\le\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n).\] The primitive outcome fourth moment and overlap imply by conditional Jensen's inequality that every retained true regression is \(L_4(P_X)\)-bounded and that \(\|\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\|_{P(\cdot\mid a,s),4}=O(1)\). The triangle inequality and the stated regression error rate then give \(\max_{f,a,s,k}\|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(1)\); no separate true- or fitted-regression envelope is assumed. For each residual term, clipping, the Lipschitz bound for \((u,v)\mapsto u/v\) on \([\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]^2\), and Hölder's inequality yield \[\left\|\mathbf 1_{a,s}\left(\frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}-\frac{p_{g,1}}{p_{a,s}}\right)(\Delta Y_k-m_{a,s,k})\right\|_{P,2}\le C_\varepsilon\left(\|\widetilde p_{g,1}-p_{g,1}\|_{P_X,4}+\|\widetilde p_{a,s}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}\right)\|\Delta Y_k-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P(\cdot\mid a,s),4}=O_P(a_n),\] and \[\left\|\mathbf 1_{a,s}\frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}(\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k})\right\|_{P,2}\le C_\varepsilon\|\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,2}=O_P(b_n).\] The fitted target-contrast term is bounded by the sum of its four regression errors. Conditional score bias is bounded by \(C_\varepsilon\max_{p,m}\|\widehat p-p\|_{P_X,2}\|\widehat m-m\|_{P_X,2}=O_P(a_nb_n)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\); foldwise independence makes every centered validation-fold plug-in fluctuation \(o_P(1)\) after \(n^{-1/2}\) summation. The empirical target share is root-\(n\) consistent, lies in the interior clipping region with probability tending to one, and its ratio expansion supplies exactly the target-share term in \(\Psi\). Therefore, uniformly over the fixed score coordinates, \[\sqrt n\{\widehat\mu-B\Theta(P)\}=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi(O_i)+o_P(1),\qquad \max_{1\le j\le M}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat\Psi_{i,j}-\Psi_j(O_i)\}^2=o_P(1).\]
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a coordinate \(j=(k,c)\), write \(k=(g,t)\), and abbreviate \(I_{a,s}=\mathbf 1\{G_i=a,S_i=s\}\). Constants below may depend on the fixed objects \(F,T,\mathcal K,M,\varepsilon,C_4\), but not on \(n\).

First derive the regression envelopes. The inequality
\[
 |\Delta Y_{i,k}|^4
 \le 8\{|Y_{it}|^4+|Y_{i,g-1}|^4\}
 \le16\max_{u\in\mathcal T}|Y_{iu}|^4
\]
and the fourth-moment assumption imply \(E_P|\Delta Y_{i,k}|^4\le16C_4\). Conditional Jensen's inequality gives, on each retained cell,
\[
 |m_{a,s,k}(x)|^4
 \le E_P[|\Delta Y_{i,k}|^4\mid G_i=a,S_i=s,X_i=x].
\]
Because \(p_{a,s}(x)\ge\varepsilon\), integration with respect to \(P_X\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,4}^4
 &\le \int E_P[|\Delta Y_{i,k}|^4\mid a,s,X_i=x],dP_X(x)\\
 &\le \varepsilon^{-1}E_P[I_{a,s}|\Delta Y_{i,k}|^4]
 \le16C_4/\varepsilon.
\end{aligned}
\]
The same calculation under the conditional law of a retained cell, together with \(|u-v|^4\le8(|u|^4+|v|^4)\), gives
\[
 \|\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\|_{P(\cdot\mid a,s),4}=O(1).
\]
The regression error condition and the triangle inequality then imply, uniformly over the fixed folds and retained indices,
\[
 \|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}\|_{P_X,4}
 \le \|m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,4}
 +\|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,4}
 =O_P(1).
\]
Thus neither a true- nor a fitted-regression envelope is an extra hypothesis.

Next consider clipping. The four retained events \((g,0),(g,1),(c,0),(c,1)\) are distinct and belong to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ret}}\). Hence \(L_{\mathrm{ret}}\ge4\), and the overlap domain \(0<\varepsilon<L_{\mathrm{ret}}^{-1}\) implies \(0<\varepsilon<1/4\). Conditional overlap and disjointness further imply
\[
 \varepsilon\le p_{a,s}(x)\le1-3\varepsilon
 \le1-\varepsilon/2
\]
for each of the four cells. Hence \(C_\varepsilon(p_{a,s})=p_{a,s}\). Projection onto an interval is one-Lipschitz, so fold uniformly
\[
 \|\widetilde p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}
 \le\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n).
\]
On \([\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]^2\), the map \((u,v)\mapsto u/v\) is Lipschitz with a finite constant \(K_\varepsilon\). Hence
\[
 \left\|\frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}
       -\frac{p_{g,1}}{p_{a,s}}\right\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n).
\]
Hölder's inequality and the residual fourth-moment bound give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\left\|I_{a,s}\left(
 \frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}
 -\frac{p_{g,1}}{p_{a,s}}\right)
 \{\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\}\right\|_{P,2}\\
 &\qquad\le K_\varepsilon\left(
 \|\widetilde p_{g,1}-p_{g,1}\|_{P_X,4}
 +\|\widetilde p_{a,s}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}\right)
 \|\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\|_{P(\cdot\mid a,s),4}
 =O_P(a_n),
\end{aligned}
\]
and bounded clipping gives
\[
 \left\|I_{a,s}\frac{\widetilde p_{g,1}}{\widetilde p_{a,s}}
 \{\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k}\}\right\|_{P,2}
 \le K_\varepsilon\|\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,2}
 =O_P(b_n).
\]
The fitted contrast error \(\widehat d_{k,c}-d_{k,c}\) is a signed sum of four regression errors and is therefore \(O_P(b_n)\) in \(L_4(P_X)\).

Define the oracle numerator summand
\[
 A_j(O_i)=I_{g,1}d_{k,c}(X_i)
 +p_{g,1}(X_i)\sum_{a,s}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}
 \frac{I_{a,s}}{p_{a,s}(X_i)}
 \{\Delta Y_{i,k}-m_{a,s,k}(X_i)\},
\]
where the sum is over the four retained cells, and let \(\widehat A_{i,j}\) be the fitted summand in Definition \(\ref{def:joint-estimator}\). The preceding bounds imply, conditionally on each training sample,
\[
 \|\widehat A_{i,j}-A_j(O_i)\|_{P,2}=O_P(a_n+b_n)=o_P(1).
\]
There is also an exact orthogonality calculation. Put \(e_{a,s}=\widehat m_{a,s,k}-m_{a,s,k}\). Conditional residual centering gives
\[
 E_P[\widehat A_{i,j}-A_j(O_i)\mid X_i=x]
 =\sum_{a,s}\sigma_{a,s}^{g,c}
 \left\{p_{g,1}(x)-\widetilde p_{g,1}(x)
 \frac{p_{a,s}(x)}{\widetilde p_{a,s}(x)}\right\}e_{a,s}(x).
\]
The bracket has \(L_4(P_X)\) norm at most a constant times the relevant propensity errors. Hölder's inequality thus gives, fold uniformly,
\[
 \left|E_P[\widehat A_{i,j}-A_j(O_i)\mid\text{training sample}]\right|
 =O_P(a_nb_n)=o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\]

Condition on the training sample for a validation fold. Foldwise independence and conditional Chebyshev's inequality show that the centered sum of \(\widehat A_{i,j}-A_j(O_i)\), divided by \(\sqrt n\), has conditional variance bounded by a fixed multiple of \(\|\widehat A_j-A_j\|_{P,2}^2=o_P(1)\). The preceding conditional-bias bound controls its mean. Since \(F\) is fixed, summing across folds gives
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat A_{i,j}-A_j(O_i)\}=o_P(1).
\]

Let \(\bar I_g=n^{-1}\sum_i I_{g,1}\) and \(\pi=\pi_{g,1}\). Overlap gives \(\pi\in[\varepsilon,1-3\varepsilon]\). Bernoulli variance and Chebyshev's inequality give \(\bar I_g-\pi=O_P(n^{-1/2})\); consequently target-share clipping is inactive with probability tending to one. Lemma \(\ref{lem:causal-identification}\) and residual centering give
\[
 E_PA_j=\pi\Theta_k(P),
 \qquad
 A_j(O_i)-\Theta_k(P)I_{g,1}=\pi\Psi_j(O_i).
\]
On the event where clipping is inactive,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\mu_j-\Theta_k(P)\}
 &=\frac{n^{-1/2}\sum_i\{A_j(O_i)-\Theta_k(P)I_{g,1}\}}{\bar I_g}
   +\frac{n^{-1/2}\sum_i\{\widehat A_{i,j}-A_j(O_i)\}}{\bar I_g}\\
 &=\frac{\pi}{\bar I_g}\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)+o_P(1)\\
 &=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)+o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
The last equality uses \(\bar I_g/\pi\to_P1\) and \(n^{-1/2}\sum_i\Psi_j(O_i)=O_P(1)\), the latter following from the finite second moment supplied by the derived residual bounds and overlap. Fixed \(M\) permits stacking:
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\mu-B\Theta(P)\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi(O_i)+o_P(1).
\]

Finally compare the fitted and oracle influence coordinates. On the same event, their difference is a finite sum of: the denominator error \(\bar I_g^{-1}-\pi^{-1}\); the fitted-contrast error; the centering error \(\widehat\mu_j-\Theta_k(P)\); a propensity-ratio error times a true residual; and a bounded fitted ratio times a regression error. Conditional Markov's inequality, foldwise independence, and the bounds already proved yield
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat\Psi_{i,j}-\Psi_j(O_i)\}^2
 \le O_P(1)\{(\bar I_g-\pi)^2
 +|\widehat\mu_j-\Theta_k(P)|^2+a_n^2+b_n^2\}=o_P(1).
\]
Here the empirical second moments of oracle residual terms are \(O_P(1)\), and the expansion just proved implies \(\widehat\mu_j-\Theta_k(P)=O_P(n^{-1/2})\). Taking the maximum over the fixed \(M\) coordinates proves the second assertion.
statements.justification: This lemma performs the score-specific DML calculation and now derives both regression envelopes from primitive moments, overlap, and the stated regression error rate.
statements.gap: Generic cross-fitting machinery does not establish the specialized clipped ratio-adjusted staggered-DDD expansion or model-specific learner achievability; the theorem remains conditional on explicit learner rates.
statements.consumer: The covariance lemma receives empirical L2 fitted-score convergence, and the joint theorem receives the asymptotic linear expansion, without assuming either conclusion or a redundant envelope.

statements.statement: Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\mathcal K\), and \(M\). For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\) with \(P=Q_O\), impose the theorem-level foldwise independence, propensity and regression \(L_4(P_X)\) rates, and product-rate condition. No separate true- or fitted-regression envelope is imposed: the score-expansion lemma derives the required envelopes from the primitive outcome fourth moment, overlap, and the regression error rate. That lemma gives \(D_{i,j}=\widehat\Psi_{i,j}-\Psi_j(O_i)\) with \(\max_j n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,j}^2=o_P(1)\). For every \(1\le j,q\le M\), \[\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}_{jq}-\Omega_{jq}=\left\{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)\Psi_q(O_i)-\Omega_{jq}\right\}+n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nD_{i,j}\widehat\Psi_{i,q}+n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)D_{i,q}.\] The oracle empirical-covariance fluctuation is \(o_P(1)\) by i.i.d. sampling and the derived fourth-moment bound. Cauchy--Schwarz gives \[\begin{aligned}|\widehat\Omega^{\mathrm{raw}}_{jq}-\Omega_{jq}|&\le\left|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi_j(O_i)\Psi_q(O_i)-\Omega_{jq}\right|\\&\quad+\left(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,j}^2\right)^{1/2}\left(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Psi_{i,q}^2\right)^{1/2}+\left(n^{-1}\sum_i\Psi_j(O_i)^2\right)^{1/2}\left(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,q}^2\right)^{1/2}=o_P(1).\end{aligned}\] Since \(M\) is fixed, \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le M\max_{j,q}|A_{jq}|\) passes entrywise convergence to operator norm. Because \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^M\) and positive-semidefinite projection is nonexpansive in Frobenius norm, \[\|\widehat\Omega-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1),\qquad \|\widehat\Omega_\lambda-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|\widehat\Omega-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\lambda_n=o_P(1).\]
statements.justification: This supporting lemma derives consistency of the exact full fitted-score covariance from the revised score expansion.
statements.gap: The DDD-specific content is verifying covariance consistency for the displayed clipped, ratio-adjusted, cross-fitted score with shared units, conditional on the explicit learner rates.
statements.consumer: The feasible joint limit theorem can continuously invert the projected and ridged covariance without assuming covariance consistency or a redundant regression envelope.

statements.statement:
Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal K\subseteq\{(g,t):2\le g\le t\le T\}\), and \(M\). Fix a law \(Q\in\mathcal M\), let \(P=Q_O\), and fix supplied sequences of off-fold learners satisfying foldwise independence, \(\max_{f,a,s}\|\widehat p_{a,s,-f}-p_{a,s}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(a_n)\), \(\max_{f,a,s,k}\|\widehat m_{a,s,k,-f}-m_{a,s,k}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(b_n)\), \(a_n\to0\), \(b_n\to0\), and \(a_nb_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). All stochastic orders, limits, and probabilities below are pointwise for this fixed pair consisting of \(Q\) and the supplied learner sequences. No existence of such learners uniformly over \(\mathcal M\), and no uniform coverage over \(\mathcal M\), is asserted. No fitted-regression envelope is separately assumed, because it follows from the primitive outcome fourth moment, overlap, and the regression error rate. Use the deterministic ridge \(\lambda_n=n^{-1/4}>0\). The everywhere-defined estimator in Definition \(\ref{def:joint-estimator}\) then satisfies
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}-\Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)\}
=\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n(b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\Psi(O_i)+o_P(1)
\rightsquigarrow N(0,V_{\mathrm{joint}}),
\qquad
\|\widehat\Omega-\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1).
\]
Moreover, \(b^{\mathrm{joint}}\) is the unique minimizer of \(b^{\prime}\Omega b\) over constant \(b\in\mathbb R^M\) satisfying \(B^{\prime}b=\omega\), \(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}\to_Pb^{\mathrm{joint}}\), \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}\to_PV_{\mathrm{joint}}>0\), and
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}P\{\tau_\omega(Q)\in\mathcal C_{n,1-\alpha}\}=1-\alpha.
\]
This is conditional pointwise inference and finite-dimensional constrained-GMM optimality within the constant span of the retained pairwise staggered-DDD scores, supported by the model-specific clipped cross-fitted score expansion. It is not an efficient influence function or a semiparametric efficiency bound for the full conditional-moment model. If a target coordinate has \(g=2\), its score and fitted score use \(\Delta Y_{i,k}=Y_{it}-Y_{i1}\). If \(\mathcal K=\{k\}\), the joint loading, estimator, and variance reduce to the published within-\(k\) comparison-cohort GMM objects. The zero-variance convention in Definition \(\ref{def:wald-interval}\) totalizes the finite-sample interval and is asymptotically inactive.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix the pair consisting of \(Q\) and the supplied learner sequences. Because a retained score contains the four distinct cells \((g,0),(g,1),(c,0),(c,1)\), the retained-cell definition gives \(L_{\mathrm{ret}}\ge4\). The corrected overlap domain therefore implies \(0<\varepsilon<1/4\), and overlap with the other three cells gives the per-score upper bound \(p_{a,s}\le1-3\varepsilon\). Hence the clipping and moment arguments in Lemmas \(\ref{lem:cross-fitted-score-expansion}\) and \(\ref{lem:fitted-covariance-consistency}\) apply pointwise to this fixed pair and give
\[
Z_n:=\sqrt n\{\widehat\mu-B\Theta(P)\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\Psi(O_i)+o_P(1),
\qquad
\widehat\Omega\to_P\Omega,
\qquad
\widehat\Omega_\lambda\to_P\Omega.
\]
These conclusions derive the needed fitted-score and covariance behavior from the displayed learner-rate hypotheses; they do not construct the learners.

Each column of \(B\) has a nonempty row support, and the supports of distinct columns are disjoint. Thus \(B\) has full column rank. The score-spectrum assumption makes \(\Omega\) positive definite, so \(B^{\prime}\Omega^{-1}B\) is positive definite. Continuity of matrix inversion at positive-definite matrices yields
\[
\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}
=\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B
 (B^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B)^{-1}\omega
\to_P
\Omega^{-1}B(B^{\prime}\Omega^{-1}B)^{-1}\omega
=b^{\mathrm{joint}}.
\]
For every sample, \(\widehat\Omega_\lambda\) is positive definite because \(\widehat\Omega\) is positive semidefinite and \(\lambda_n>0\). The same full-rank argument makes \(B^{\prime}\widehat\Omega_\lambda^{-1}B\) positive definite. Together with propensity and target-share clipping, this proves that every denominator and inverse in \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}\) is defined for every realized sample. Direct multiplication also gives
\[
B^{\prime}\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}=\omega.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}-\Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)\}
&=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}
  \sqrt n\{\widehat\mu-B\Theta(P)\}\\
&=(b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\frac1{\sqrt n}
  \sum_{i=1}^n\Psi(O_i)+o_P(1),
\end{aligned}
\]
because \(Z_n=O_P(1)\) and \(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}}=o_P(1)\).

Put \(Z_i=(b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\Psi(O_i)\). By independent sampling and Lemma \(\ref{lem:causal-identification}\), the \(Z_i\) are independent and identically distributed with mean zero and variance
\[
E_P[Z_i^2]=(b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{joint}}=V_{\mathrm{joint}}.
\]
The fourth-moment and overlap derivations in Lemma \(\ref{lem:cross-fitted-score-expansion}\) imply \(E_P|\Psi_j(O_i)|^4<\infty\) for every fixed coordinate, and fixed \(M\) therefore gives \(E_P|Z_i|^4<\infty\). For \(Z_{n,i}=Z_i/\sqrt n\),
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Var}(Z_{n,i})=V_{\mathrm{joint}},
\]
and, for every \(r>0\),
\[
\sum_{i=1}^nE_P[Z_{n,i}^2\mathbf 1\{|Z_{n,i}|>r\}]
=E_P[Z_i^2\mathbf 1\{|Z_i|>r\sqrt n\}]
\le\frac{E_P[Z_i^4]}{r^2n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The Lindeberg--Feller theorem in Lemma \(\ref{lem:lindeberg-feller-central-limit}\) gives
\[
\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^nZ_i\rightsquigarrow N(0,V_{\mathrm{joint}}).
\]
To absorb the remainder directly, if \(r_n=o_P(1)\), then for every \(h>0\) and every continuity point \(x\) of the limiting normal distribution,
\[
P(X_n\le x-h)-P(|r_n|>h)
\le P(X_n+r_n\le x)
\le P(X_n\le x+h)+P(|r_n|>h),
\]
where \(X_n=n^{-1/2}\sum_iZ_i\). Taking limits and then \(h\downarrow0\) proves the asserted limit law.

It remains to establish the finite-span optimum. Consider the Lagrangian
\[
\mathcal L(b,\lambda)=b^{\prime}\Omega b
-2\lambda^{\prime}(B^{\prime}b-\omega).
\]
Its first-order conditions are \(b=\Omega^{-1}B\lambda\) and \(B^{\prime}b=\omega\), whence
\[
\lambda=(B^{\prime}\Omega^{-1}B)^{-1}\omega,
\qquad
b=\Omega^{-1}B(B^{\prime}\Omega^{-1}B)^{-1}\omega
=b^{\mathrm{joint}}.
\]
Strict convexity of \(b\mapsto b^{\prime}\Omega b\) makes this feasible solution the unique minimizer. Because \(\mathbf 1^{\prime}\omega=1\), the constraint \(B^{\prime}b^{\mathrm{joint}}=\omega\) implies \(b^{\mathrm{joint}}\ne0\). The spectrum bound then gives
\[
V_{\mathrm{joint}}
=(b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{joint}}
\ge\kappa\|b^{\mathrm{joint}}\|_2^2>0.
\]

The already-proved convergences of the loading and covariance imply
\[
\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}
=(\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}
 \widehat\Omega\widehat b^{\mathrm{joint}}
\to_PV_{\mathrm{joint}}.
\]
Lemma \(\ref{lem:causal-identification}\) gives \(\tau_\omega(Q)=\Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)\). Hence
\[
\frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}-\tau_\omega(Q)\}}
     {\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}}}
\rightsquigarrow N(0,1).
\]
Indeed, \(\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{joint}}/\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}}-1=o_P(1)\), and multiplying this error by the tight unstudentized standardized statistic is \(o_P(1)\); the same distribution-function sandwich used above transfers the limit. Continuity of the standard normal distribution at \(\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\) now proves
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}P\{\tau_\omega(Q)\in\mathcal C_{n,1-\alpha}\}=1-\alpha.
\]
Since \(V_{\mathrm{joint}}>0\) and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}\to_PV_{\mathrm{joint}}\), the event \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{joint}}=0\) has probability tending to zero, so the finite-sample zero-variance convention is asymptotically inactive.

When \(g=2\), the outcome-change definition gives \(\Delta Y_{i,k}=Y_{it}-Y_{i1}\) in both oracle and fitted scores. If \(\mathcal K=\{k\}\), then \(B=\mathbf 1\) and \(\omega_k=1\), so
\[
b^{\mathrm{joint}}
=\frac{\Omega^{-1}\mathbf 1}{\mathbf 1^{\prime}\Omega^{-1}\mathbf 1}
=b^{\mathrm{sep}}.
\]
The feasible loading, estimator, and variance formulas reduce accordingly. Every conclusion is pointwise for the fixed law/learner pair and confined to the finite constant retained-score span; no tangent-space or full semiparametric-efficiency assertion has been used.
statements.justification: It supplies an everywhere-defined feasible statistic, a derived unit-level limit law, and exact Wald coverage for the final causal aggregate within the retained constant score span.
statements.gap: Hsieh validates unit-level covariance aggregation under fixed stack weights; this theorem estimates a joint covariance-optimal loading within the retained covariate-adjusted pairwise-score span, conditional on supplied learner rates.
statements.consumer: Applied staggered-DDD event studies obtain a joint point estimator and fully specified Wald interval, with no claim of a full semiparametric bound or uniform learner achievability.

statements.statement:
Fix \(F\), \(T\), \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal K\subseteq\{(g,t):2\le g\le t\le T\}\), and \(M\). The aggregate formed from the Ortiz-Villavicencio--Sant'Anna componentwise-GMM ATT functionals using the prespecified weights is joint-optimal in the constant retained-score span if and only if \(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}=0\), equivalently if and only if each block of \(\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}\) is constant across the comparison cohorts in that block. For every \(Q\in\mathcal M\), with \(P=Q_O\), the population identity
\[
V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}
=(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}})^{\prime}(N^{\prime}\Omega N)^{-1}(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}})
=(b^{\mathrm{sep}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}})^{\prime}\Omega(b^{\mathrm{sep}}-b^{\mathrm{joint}})
\]
holds without learner conditions, with the zero-dimensional quadratic interpreted as zero. Suppose in addition that the i.i.d. sampling, fixed-fold sample splitting, propensity and regression \(L_4(P_X)\) rates, product-rate condition, and deterministic ridge condition of Theorem \(\ref{thm:joint-system-limit}\) all hold. The learner sequences and rates are theorem-level conditional hypotheses, and no uniform learner-achievability claim over \(\mathcal M\) is made; no separate fitted-regression envelope is required. Then \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{joint}}\) and \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sep}}\) have asymptotic variances \(V_{\mathrm{joint}}\) and \(V_{\mathrm{sep}}\), respectively, so the joint estimator has strictly smaller asymptotic variance exactly when the net cross-block covariance contribution is nonconstant across comparison cohorts within at least one group-event block. Moreover, \(\widehat\Delta\ge0\) for every realized sample and \(\widehat\Delta\to_P V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}\). Thus \(\widehat\Delta\) is a consistent descriptive diagnostic of the constant retained-score-span efficiency loss; no convergence rate, test, confidence interval, or full semiparametric-efficiency claim is made. For \(g=2\), all covariance entries use the defined baseline period \(1\). If \(\mathcal K=\{k\}\), then \(N^{\prime}\Omega b^{\mathrm{sep}}=0\), \(b^{\mathrm{joint}}=b^{\mathrm{sep}}\), and \(V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}=0\), reproducing within-cell GMM optimality.
statements.justification: It gives the exact finite-span equality criterion, variance-gap quadratic, and consistency of the feasible descriptive loss diagnostic.
statements.gap: The DDD-specific result maps standard constrained GMM/SUR algebra to the retained shared-cell score system and isolates nonconstant net cross-block covariance across comparison coordinates as the exact strict-gain mechanism.
statements.consumer: Researchers can compare the published componentwise aggregate with the joint finite-span estimator and report \(\widehat\Delta\) descriptively, without interpreting the result as covariate-varying conditional-precision efficiency.

statements.statement: Which label-preserving equivalence classes of sufficient invariants \(\mathfrak H(P)=(\mathcal I,(\mathcal J_k)_k,\mathcal R,A,\omega,\mathfrak C(P),N)\) satisfy \(N^{\prime}\mathfrak C(P)b^{\mathrm{sep}}(P)=0\), and which admit a bounded compatible full-data law \(Q\in\mathcal M\), with \(P=Q_O\), for which this vector is nonzero? Because \(\mathfrak C(P)=\Omega(P)\) and \(N\) is canonically determined by the labelled comparison sets, the displayed vector is determined by \(\mathfrak H(P)\); no claim is made from an unlabelled overlap graph. As a concrete construct-and-determine subquestion, take \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2),(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3,\infty\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{\infty\}\), and prespecified nonzero \(\omega\). Construct a bounded compatible \(Q\) whose resulting \(3\times3\) covariance \(\Omega\) is positive definite, calculate \(V_{\mathrm{sep}}-V_{\mathrm{joint}}\) exactly, and determine whether it can be strictly positive. The handle is the labelled residual-incidence and compatible covariance parameterization in \(\mathrm{Def.}\) \(\ref{def:labelled-incidence-handle}\).
statements.justification: The sufficient labelled invariant makes the equality diagnostic mathematically determined and turns the smallest reused-cell architecture into an explicit compatible-law construction problem.
statements.gap: Zellner's systems geometry and Hansen's GMM theory do not classify DDD systems by score labels, signed residual incidences, prespecified aggregate weights, and compatible covariance maps; the staggered-DDD literature gives no such sufficient-invariant criterion or exact smallest strict-gap construction.
statements.consumer: A study designer can combine the prespecified cohort-event architecture with a compatible covariance specification to determine whether componentwise aggregation is certified or whether a strict joint-loading gain must be assessed.

sampling_model.design: Observational staggered triple differences with a fixed balanced-panel horizon and absorbing enabling dates.
sampling_model.units: \(W_1,\ldots,W_n\) are independent full-data draws from \(Q\); the statistic observes only \(O_i=o(W_i)\), whose law is \(P=Q_O\).
sampling_model.treatment: Under \(Q\), \(G_i\in\mathcal G\cup\{\infty\}\) with \(\mathcal G=\{2,\ldots,T\}\); eligible units become treated at finite \(G_i\), while ineligible potential outcomes do not vary with enabling date.
sampling_model.overlap: Under \(Q\), every retained cohort-eligibility cell has conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\), where \(0<\varepsilon<1/4\), for \(Q_X\)-almost every covariate value.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold cross-fitting uses validation observations independent of their training fits. Raw propensity errors are \(O_P(a_n)\) in \(L_4(P_X)\), regression errors are \(O_P(b_n)\) in \(L_4(P_X)\), fitted regressions have a uniform fourth-moment envelope, and \(a_nb_n=o(n^{-1/2})\). Every fitted propensity and empirical target share is clipped by \(C_\varepsilon\); the unit-level covariance is projected onto the positive-semidefinite cone and regularized by \(n^{-1/4}I_M\) only for loading inversion.

Theorem 6.3 and Propositions 6.4--6.5 supply fixed-weight stacked-DDD asymptotic normality and correct original-unit covariance aggregation when comparison units recur, but do not jointly optimize the complete retained pairwise-score vector for a prespecified scalar aggregate or state its componentwise-versus-joint equality frontier.

tldr: The causal aggregate is defined under a full-data law \(Q\), uses only target coordinates \(2\le g\le t\le T\), and is identified by an explicit observed-data functional of \(P=Q_O\). Published staggered-DDD GMM optimizes every group-time ATT separately and only then forms an event-study aggregate, while stacked DDD already provides valid unit-level variance aggregation when comparison units recur across stacks. Shared eligible and ineligible comparison units also make zero-sum comparison contrasts from one group-event cell informative for another. The two closed contributions are an everywhere-defined clipped and ridged joint estimator with a derived studentized limit law, and an exact frontier showing when componentwise GMM aggregation loses variance to joint covariance weighting. Supporting results exhibit a nonempty feasible-overlap law, establish causal identification, expand the shared-cell covariance, derive the exact cross-fitted score expansion from \(L_4\) and product-rate hypotheses, and pass that expansion to fixed-dimensional fitted-score covariance consistency. The open question classifies law-sufficient labelled incidence invariants and asks for an exact bounded three-cohort/two-event strict-gap construction.

project_justification.gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna prove minimum variance within each group-time comparison block and then aggregate. Hsieh proves valid fixed-weight stacked-DDD inference with reused comparison units. Neither result checks whether blockwise optimization remains optimal for the final covariate-adjusted DDD aggregate when all admissible comparison-cohort scores are retained jointly.
project_justification.niche: The repeated-cell structure creates a causal version of seemingly unrelated equations: other group-event blocks contain mean-zero overidentifying contrasts that can reduce the variance of the reported scalar without changing its event-study weights.
project_justification.fill: A separate supporting reduction identifies the full-data causal aggregate \(\tau_\omega(Q)\) with the displayed observed-data functional \(\Theta_\omega^{\mathrm{agg}}(P)\). The joint incidence-constrained GMM construction then uses only \(P\), explicitly clipped propensities, a projected and ridged covariance, and an exact studentized interval. A bounded four-cell construction demonstrates feasibility when \(0<\varepsilon<1/4\). A score-specific argument uses foldwise independence, outcome, true-regression, and fitted-regression fourth-moment control, separate propensity and regression \(L_4\) errors, and their explicit \(o(n^{-1/2})\) product to derive asymptotic linearity and empirical score convergence. The entrywise covariance argument then derives operator-norm consistency. The if-and-only-if collapse frontier and quadratic variance-gap functional compare joint loading with the published componentwise plug-in without recasting shared-unit variance aggregation as new.

related_work: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025, Theorem 4.1, Corollary 4.1, and Remark 4.6) supply the pairwise staggered-DDD scores and the componentwise constant-GMM estimator that Theorem 2 strictly tightens for a prespecified aggregate. Hsieh (2026, arXiv:2604.22982v1, Section 6) is a close stacked-DDD comparator. Its Theorem 6.3 derives fixed-weight stacked event-study asymptotic normality, Proposition 6.4 includes covariance from comparison units reused across stacks, and Proposition 6.5 consistently estimates that variance by aggregating influence contributions at the original-unit level before squaring. Theorem 1 therefore does not claim that Hsieh ignores cross-stack dependence; it differs by estimating a full covariance-weighted loading over all retained covariate-adjusted comparison-cohort scores and by totalizing the resulting inverses and interval. The supporting score-expansion and covariance-consistency lemmas are derived directly from the displayed clipped score, fourth-moment envelopes, fixed-fold sample splitting, separate \(L_4\) nuisance errors, and the explicit product rate; neither matrix result is attributed to Hsieh. Theorem 2 supplies the joint-versus-componentwise equality frontier and loss identity absent from Hsieh's fixed-stack aggregation, which Hsieh presents as complementary to GMM and as trading efficiency for transparency. Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025, Theorems 3.2 and 4.1) inform joint covariance weighting in staggered two-way difference-in-differences, but their moment system has no eligibility-domain contrast. Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami (2025, Theorems 5 and 7) inform canonical two-period DDD score algebra. Zellner (1962), Hansen (1982), and Ackerberg, Chen, Hahn, and Liao (2014) supply systems, finite-dimensional GMM, and two-step semiparametric geometry; they are methodological inputs rather than novelty targets. Chernozhukov et al. (2018) supports generic cross-fitting and orthogonal product-rate machinery only; the clipped ratio-score bounds are derived here term by term.
technical_internal_limitation: The joint optimum is an efficiency statement within the constant linear span of the retained pairwise doubly robust score vector. It is not the semiparametric efficiency bound for the full conditional-moment DDD model.
honest_scope: The full-data law \(Q\) defines potential outcomes and the causal target, while every score, nuisance, covariance, estimator, and limit calculation is a functional of the observed-data pushforward \(P=Q_O\); the bridge between them is the supporting identification lemma. Treated cohorts lie in \(\mathcal G=\{2,\ldots,T\}\), every target coordinate satisfies \(2\le g\le t\le T\), and \(g=2\) uses baseline period \(1\). The common overlap domain is the feasible interval \(0<\varepsilon<1/4\), and the explicit four-cell law proves that the primitive class can be nonempty. The two theorems fix the panel horizon, target support, comparison sets, and event-study weights. Their learner hypotheses are procedure-level: foldwise independence, fourth-moment envelopes, separate \(L_4\) propensity and regression consistency, and an explicit \(o(n^{-1/2})\) product rate. They exclude data-adaptive target weights, singular population score covariance, growing numbers of cohorts, unbalanced panels, and repeated cross-sections. Pairwise identification and valid unit-level variance aggregation for reused comparison units are published supporting structure; score convergence, asymptotic linearity, and covariance consistency for the exact fitted score are derived supporting conclusions, not premises or separate novelty claims. If cross-block score covariance is zero, joint and componentwise loadings coincide; if \(|\mathcal K|=1\), both reduce to the published within-block GMM loading and the variance gap is zero. The new closed content is the totalized joint estimator and joint-versus-componentwise frontier within the retained score span. Classification by the sufficient labelled invariant, including whether the specified three-cohort/two-event architecture admits an exact positive-definite strict-gap law, is open; no conclusion is asserted from unlabelled overlap alone.
